items.title: Saudi Hotel Builders Keep Going as Attacks Scare Off Foreign Visitors
items.summary: Saudi hotel developers are still building through Houthi attacks, and a record pipeline shows it. But their bet rests on domestic and religious travel. The international guests that Vision 2030 needs are the ones the attacks are scaring off.

items.title: Loyalty Unscripted: Relationship or Commodity?
items.summary: Airline loyalty programs must make rewards easier to use while protecting the commercial value of the seats customers redeem.

items.title: Redefining Flying: Where Innovation Meets the Human Touch
items.summary: Airlines seeking more premium revenue must decide how to allocate limited cabin space between higher-value seats, traditional amenities, and new passenger experiences.

items.title: One Night in Bangkok: Eurovision Asia Tests Thailand’s Bet on Events
items.summary: Thailand wants events to offset falling arrivals. Early data shows Eurovision Asia riding Bangkok's seasonal upswing, not driving it. One night won't move the needle, but a steady calendar of events just might.

items.title: Boeing on Market Forces Shaping Fleets and Routes Through 2045
items.summary: Aviation's next phase of growth will require airlines, manufacturers, and airports to make long-term investment decisions around sharply different regional demand patterns.

items.title: Expedia Confirms Cyberattack Through Third-Party Vendor
items.summary: Expedia says attackers reached its systems through a compromised technology provider. The company has not disclosed the extent of any data exposure.

items.title: How Embraer and Porter Airlines Consider Matching the Jet to the Market
items.summary: Airlines choosing new aircraft must weigh lower per-seat operating costs against the revenue consequences of deploying more capacity than a market can support.

items.title: Flight Attendants Union Chief Targets Regional Pay, Delta, and Worker Data
items.summary: The era of catch-up flight attendant raises is ending, but airlines shouldn’t expect labor costs to ease. The next fights are over regional pay and worker data.
